text: It is 1987 and I am on a ferry from Belgium to England. Suddenly, the ferry starts tilting and water begins to pour in. I and many other passengers are trying to get to the deck by a rope ladder. I climb up the ladder and stand on the deck, looking at the 20 other passengers making their way up behind me. Directly below me, a man who is midway up the ladder seems frozen into immobility by fear or cold and is blocking the way. I try to speak and reach to him, but he does not react. People behind me are jostling. The ship seems to be sinking fast and the man is still blocking the ladder. I have a gun in my possession. From the crowd below, someone shouts that I should shoot the man to make him fall off. If I shoot the man, he will probably die from the shot, but the 19 other people will be able to climb on deck. If I do not shoot the man, he will probably continue blocking the way so that many of the people behind me will not be able to get on deck and therefore will drown.
